prompt: Which statement correctly gives the definition of a systematic error according to the Cambridge 9702 syllabus?
options: An unpredictable variation in repeated measurements that causes readings to scatter about the true value.
An error that causes measurements to be consistently offset from the true value in the same direction.
The difference between the maximum and minimum values obtained in a set of repeated measurements.
An arithmetic blunder made when entering experimental data into a calculation.

answer.explanation: A systematic error is defined as an error that causes measurements to be consistently offset from the true value in the same direction.

distractor_explanations: This is the syllabus definition of a random error.
Correct. Systematic errors consistently shift readings in one direction away from the true value.
This describes the range or spread of a set of readings.
Arithmetic blunders or typos are personal mistakes, not systematic experimental errors.
hints: Think about whether the shift occurs in a constant direction or varies unpredictably.
Recall the controlled definition: offset in the same direction.
solution: A systematic error causes measurements to be consistently offset from the true value in the same direction.
teacher_walkthrough: Recall the controlled definition from the syllabus.
Systematic errors produce a constant bias in one direction (too high or too low).

provenance.independence_statement: Authored to test verbatim recall of the Cambridge systematic error definition.
